newsitem.title: FRANCE: New Total plant blocked in French strike.
newsitem.headline: New Total plant blocked in French strike.

text.p: Oil company Total SA said on Monday that lorries had blocked its La Mede refinery near Marseille as truckers stepped up an eight-day-old pay strike.
It is the second refinery run by France's largest petrol retailer to be blocked since the strike began last week. Total's Dunkirk refinery is also blocked, a company spokesman said.
"The situation has become more complicated since last week, but it fluctuates from one moment to the next," he added.
Truckers were blocking fuel deliveries from La Mede but the refinery was operating as normal, he said.
A number of other refineries, including a nearby Shell plant at Berre and Elf's Donges plant in western France, are also hit.
Oil industry sources said most petrol stations were still getting deliveries but several were closed in the south, southwest and northwest.
Most stations run on three to five days' supply in reserve. But this is unlikely to be enough in coming days as more motorists are buying full tanks of petrol, they said.
"If the blockades last another 48 hours we'll have a much more difficult situation," the Total spokesman said.

Truckers have targeted refineries and fuel depots, blocking industrial zones in Le Havre and Rouen in the northwest, and cutting off the last petrol depot still accessible in the Pyrenees-Atlantiques region, at Boucau near Bayonne.

In the southwestern city of Bordeaux, most petrol stations had run out of supplies. Bordeaux has been singled out for one of the tightest nooses because conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe is mayor of the city.
